title: Gateway to the Americas Bridge to close overnight Nov. 17 and Nov. 19 for upgrades
excerpt: Northbound traffic at the Gateway to the Americas Bridge will halt from 2 to 4 a.m. on Nov. 17 and Nov. 19 for facility upgrades, CBP said.
content:
Northbound traffic at the Gateway to the Americas Bridge will come to a temporary halt in the early morning hours of Tuesday, Nov. 17, and Thursday, Nov. 19, as U.S. Customs and Border Protection carries out facility upgrades at the Laredo Port of Entry.

Both vehicular and pedestrian traffic heading north will be stopped from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. on each of the two mornings, CBP said in a release issued Nov. 11. Traffic is expected to resume at about 4 a.m. on both days.

The Gateway to the Americas Bridge — Bridge I — is the downtown crossing between Laredo and Nuevo Laredo, used heavily by pedestrians and daily crossers. A two-hour overnight closure is short, but anyone crossing in those early-morning hours will need to plan around it or use another bridge.

Laredo's other international crossings — the World Trade Bridge, the Juarez-Lincoln Bridge and the Colombia-Solidarity Bridge — were not named in the CBP notice, and the halt applies only to northbound traffic at the Gateway bridge during the two windows.

CBP described the work as essential facility upgrades. The agency did not detail what the upgrades involve, and the notice gave no indication of longer closures beyond the two scheduled windows.
